cinemaProjects.title: ECHOES OF LAGOS
cinemaProjects.screenplayRaw:
# ECHOES OF LAGOS

### EXT. SURULERE BACKSTREET - NIGHT <!-- scene-id: scene-01 -->

> Production Note: Shot on 35mm Panavision Anamorphic lenses (40mm wide) with a Twilight Fable color grade—deep velvety indigos in the shadows contrasted against burnt-amber highlights. Lighting is strictly motivated by a single buzzing sodium streetlamp overhead and a red "RECORDING" bulkhead bulb above the alley entrance. KOLA (20s) wears a dark slate utility overshirt over a ribbed black tank, silver chain catching faint specular flares. Camera tracks low behind him at a brisk, urgent pace.

[B-ROLL: Rain-slicked asphalt reflecting buzzing amber sodium streetlamps and drifting generator exhaust in thick indigo twilight]

Footsteps slap wet concrete. KOLA cuts sharply down a narrow Surulere alley, shoulders tense, glancing once over his shoulder into the empty gloom behind him. He grips a [PROP: Weathered Leather Satchel] tight against his ribs.

He reaches a recessed alcove and slams his palm against the cold steel of a [PROP: Heavy Steel Studio Door]. Above him, a caged red bulb flickers on, painting his sweat-beaded brow in crimson.

@KOLA
(low, breathless into the intercom)
It's me. Kill the outside light—now.

A metallic latch snaps open from within. Kola slips inside, and the heavy door seals shut behind him with the finality of a vault.

---

### INT. ANALOG CONTROL ROOM - NIGHT <!-- scene-id: scene-02 -->

> Production Note: Switch to 50mm Panavision Anamorphic lens for tight, claustrophobic framing across the console. Twilight Fable grade deepens the tungsten warmth of the desk lamps against cool slate reflections on the vocal booth glass. Lighting is motivated solely by gooseneck console lamps, backlit VU meters, and the turquoise glow of an oscilloscope. TADE (30s, sound engineer) wears a faded olive work jacket and thick-rimmed glasses catching horizontal anamorphic flares. Handheld micro-jitters build thriller tension.

The room hums with high-voltage static. TADE hunches over a [PROP: 24-Track Mixing Console], fingers poised over mute switches like detonators. Across the room, a [PROP: Reel-to-Reel Tape Machine] sits idle, threaded and waiting.

[B-ROLL: Macro anamorphic close-up of glowing amber VU meters twitching silently against brushed dark aluminum]

Suddenly, the overhead practical lamps dip—brownout. The backup inverter kicks in with a low, rhythmic throb. Kola steps out of the shadows, drops his satchel, and crosses straight toward the double-paned vocal booth glass without breaking stride.

@TADE
(pressing the talkback button, urgent)
Grid's unstable, Kola. Inverter gives us twenty minutes clean before the voltage drops. One take.

Kola steps behind the glass, sliding oversized studio headphones over one ear. He locks eyes with Tade through the reflection of glowing faders.

@KOLA
(deadpan, steady)
Roll the tape.

Tade slams the heavy record lever down. The reels catch and spin. A sharp electronic hi-hat slices through the studio monitors.

---

### INT. VOCAL BOOTH - NIGHT <!-- scene-id: scene-03 -->

> Production Note: 75mm and 100mm Panavision Anamorphic lenses for compressed, razor-sharp close-ups and whip-pan transitions. Motivated lighting from a single bare warm-tungsten Edison bulb swinging gently overhead, casting shifting thriller shadows across Kola's face while cool blue twilight spills through a high slit window. Slow, relentless push-in timed to the 128 BPM pulse of the track, escalating into rapid staccato cuts during the chorus.

Smoke from a burning incense stick curls around a [PROP: Vintage Brass Condenser Microphone]. Kola grips the pop filter stand, knuckles white, staring down the lens as the bassline drops like a thunderclap inside the padded room.

[B-ROLL: Staccato flashes of spinning magnetic tape, trembling bass speaker cones, and blurred Lagos okada headlights streaking past the high slit window]

Kola leans into the mic, veins rising in his neck, delivering his verse with coiled, rhythmic ferocity. He crumples a [PROP: Hand-Written Lyric Sheet] in his fist and lets it drop to the floor—no safety net.

@KOLA
(rhythmic, fierce, building to a crescendo)
Shadows on the Third Mainland, sirens in the rain—every beat a heartbeat, echo through the vein!

[B-ROLL: Whip-pan from Kola's glistening eyes to Tade slamming three faders upward in sync with a percussive snare hit]

The Edison bulb overhead flares brighter as the voltage surges. Kola pivots sharply around the mic, silhouette slicing through the amber haze in wide anamorphic streaks. Sweat flies off his jaw as the chorus peaks—layered harmonies reverberating off the acoustic foam.

@KOLA
(half-whispered over the sudden drop-out of the beat)
Lagos never sleeps... and neither do we.

SNAP CUT TO BLACK as Tade hits the master kill switch, leaving only the dying mechanical whirr of the tape reel echoing into silence.
